goal.title: Add the telemetry package
criteria: The same email, in any case or with spaces around it, always gives the same player ID under the same key; other emails and other keys give other IDs; an unkeyed hash of the email never equals the ID; a key under 32 characters is refused.
Every record is a single valid JSON object on its own line, with time, level, event and player first, and the email handed to the recorder never appears in its output.
A player's `player_day` record is written once per UTC day, and again on the next day.
Redacting real failing-import messages built from the repo's test battle logs and decks leaves no battle-log line, card name or player name, while the playmat's own wording survives.
A missing recorder records nothing and never fails.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/telemetry/ids.go:33-38 refuses keys under MinKey=32 (NewIDs). ids.go:43-51 lower-cases and trims the email, then returns "p_"+first 16 hex of HMAC-SHA256 under a key derived from the secret with a domain prefix, so the same key and email give the same ID and another key gives another ID. ids_test.go:27-37 pins golden IDs, ids_test.go:39-52 covers case and space variants, ids_test.go:54-64 covers other emails and other keys, ids_test.go:66-88 checks unkeyed sha256/base64/HMAC-with-nil-key guesses never match, ids_test.go:90-101 covers 31 vs 32 char keys.

recorder.go:59-75 defines the line struct with time, level, event, player as the first four fields, in that order; omitempty drops empty fields. recorder.go:132-139 marshals one object and appends a newline. Event.Email is tagged json:"-" (recorder.go:54) and is only hashed into Player (recorder.go:124); cut() (recorder.go:128-129, 169-189) removes the email from Message and Reason. recorder_test.go:56-74 checks the email, its local part and its domain never appear in output for every event constant, and recorder_test.go:28-54 checks the line format and that each line parses as JSON.

recorder.go:147-166: Active derives the UTC date (recorder.go:155), resets the seen-set when the day changes (recorder.go:157-158), and writes player_day only on first sighting of the ID in that day (recorder.go:160-164). recorder_test.go:78-100 checks one record for the same player across repeated calls and case variants on the 12th, none for the 12th 23:59:59 repeat, and a new record on 13th UTC (including a New York local time that is already 13th UTC).

redact_test.go:70-135 (TestRedactRealImportErrors) provokes four real failures via game.NewManager(...).Import using testdata/logs/2026-10-11_ledjo23_alakazam-donk.txt and testdata/decks/mega-lucario-ex-v12.txt (both exist, confirmed by glob), redacts each message against SensitiveFromJSON of the call args, and checks no leak from leaks() (player names, deck card names, every non-heading log line) survives, and that the playmat wording survives ("\"…\" before the Setup section", "for … in deck", "for … in hand", "has no … in play in the bench", "cannot tell which player owns the log"). The message texts are in internal/importer/parse.go:137 and :247. Redaction rules are in redact.go:40-81. redact_test.go:162-189 also redacts every corpus log line. The verify summary reports go test ./internal/telemetry passing; I did not re-run it. The 'survives' substrings for 'in deck' and 'in play in the bench' were not located in the source by grep, so their match depends on the runtime message text the passing test produces.

recorder.go:83-108 and 112-115 and 147-149: Record, Active and ID return early on a nil *Recorder, so nothing is written and nothing panics. recorder.go:103-108 returns "" for nil. ids.go:43-46 also handles nil *IDs. recorder_test.go:110-118 (TestNilRecorder) exercises Record, Active and ID on a nil recorder.

items.title: Switch the existing log lines to player IDs

goal.title: Switch the existing log lines to player IDs
criteria: Signing in, signing out, hitting the request limit, being refused at the user cap and letting a game expire each write a record with the player ID and without the email address.
The admin page's own log lines and its refusal lines name the admin or caller by player ID, not email.
The same account has the same ID before and after a sign-out, and from a second hosted instance started with the same key.
Hosted mode will not start without the player-ID secret, or with one shorter than 32 characters, and its start-up line says player IDs are on without showing the key.
No logger call in the hosted packages formats an account's email address, and a test fails if one is added.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: Each event has a recorder call with Email set, and the recorder writes only the hashed player ID. Sign-in: internal/hostauth/google.go:95 (sign_in_refused) and :230 (sign_in). Sign-out: internal/hostauth/board.go:131-133 (sign_out). Request limit: internal/hostauth/limit.go:85-86 (limited, reason rate). User cap: internal/usergames/usergames.go:131-133 (limited, reason places). Game expiry: usergames.go:200-202 (game_expired with idle). Writing is in internal/telemetry/recorder.go:110-140 (Email is json:"-" and only hashed into Player; cut() removes the email from Message and Reason). The cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_events_test.go:57-100 test asserts the records and checks that no email appears in records or logs.

Admin action log lines use the admin's ID: internal/cacheadmin/cacheadmin.go:196, 210, 250, 252 pass s.by(r) as the by value. The by() helper (internal/cacheadmin/handler.go:50-57) returns s.PlayerID(email) or "admin", never the email. Clear and check each pass s.by(r) to Start/CheckNow (handler.go:34, 73). The page's 'Last check' and 'Images for ... by' text is the ID (cacheadmin_test.go, events_test.go:46). Refusal lines: internal/hostauth/admin.go:42-44 and :51-53 replaced the 'refused admin ... for <email>' log lines with admin_refused records keyed by player ID. Caveat, not a log or refusal log line: the page still renders 'Signed in as {{.Email}}' (internal/cacheadmin/page.go:40), and the RequireAdmin refusal response text at admin.go:~47 reads 'You are signed in as <email>' to the refused caller. These are shown back to the user, not logged, so I did not count them against this criterion.

The ID is a deterministic keyed HMAC of the lower-cased, trimmed email with the key from TCGREPLAY_PLAYER_ID_KEY (internal/telemetry/ids.go:33-51, no per-process or per-session salt). internal/telemetry/ids_test.go:27-64 pins golden IDs and checks that the same key gives the same ID across IDs values. cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_events_test.go:102-143 (TestHostedPlayerIDStable) checks the same sign_in player ID before and after sign-out, from another assistant, and on a second startHosted instance with the same key.

cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go:139-150 (hostedRecorder) returns an error naming TCGREPLAY_PLAYER_ID_KEY and 'at least 32 characters' when telemetry.NewIDs fails (length under telemetry.MinKey=32, including empty; ids.go:33-36). newHosted calls hostedRecorder before anything listens (hosted.go:270-275), and runHosted returns that error before net.Listen (hosted.go:395-411). The start-up line at hosted.go:415 ends with 'player IDs on' and has no key. Tests: cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_events_test.go:160-191 (missing and 31-character keys exit non-zero, naming the setting, never printing the key) and :193-215 (start-up line says 'player IDs on' and does not show the key).

A grep of the logger calls in internal/hostauth, internal/usergames, internal/cacheadmin, internal/webui and cmd/tcgreplay (hosted*.go, main.go) finds no call that formats an email. The remaining logger calls are in hostauth/google.go:71-90, oauth.go, board.go:65, admin.go:36, usergames.go:290, cacheadmin.go:132-252, and hosted.go, and none passes an email. The guard is cmd/tcgreplay/noemail_test.go:14-114 (TestNoLoggerFormatsAnEmail scans the non-test files of those packages for log.*, Logf or logf calls with a .Email selector argument; TestEmailLogGuardCatchesALeak checks the detector). Limitation: the guard matches only a direct .Email selector in the arguments, so an email copied to a local variable first and then logged would not be caught. No such case exists in the current code.

items.title: Record tool calls, daily players and errors

goal.title: Record tool calls, daily players and errors
criteria: After a sign-in, an import through a named assistant and a new game, there is a record for each sign-in, tool call (with the tool and assistant), import and new game, each with a time and the same player ID.
Two players, one active twice and one once in a day, produce exactly two `player_day` records for that day, alongside their tool-call, import and new-game records.
A failing import (a malformed battle log) writes an error record naming the tool, the error message and the player ID; a failing board action writes one naming the action.
Across a whole session, the records contain none of: the test player's email or display name, any Google token value, any line of the pasted battle log, any card name from the decks.
A request refused by the rate limit is recorded once, as a limit refusal, not as a tool call.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: hostauth/google.go:230-231 records sign_in with the account email (Recorder.Record hashes it to the player field, recorder.go:124). usergames/telemetry.go:47-50 records tool_call for every tools/call with Tool, Assistant (from the session client name via mcpserver.AssistantName) and the token's account; :62 and :64 record import and new_game with the same player and Assistant. Each line carries time (recorder.go:121) and the player ID is the same HMAC of the email (ids.go:43-51). cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_usage_test.go:119-160 asserts sign_in, tool_call (import_log and new_game, assistant Claude), import and new_game for the same aID.

usergames/usergames.go:119-122 calls r.cfg.Recorder.Active(acct.Email) in Use; telemetry.go Active (recorder.go:147-166) writes player_day only on a player's first activity per UTC day (per-day seen set). cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_usage_test.go:234-269 (TestHostedDailyPlayers) has A act twice and B once on 2026-11-12 and asserts exactly two player_day records, one for aID and one for bID, plus tool_call, import and new_game records for each. internal/usergames/telemetry_test.go:232-269 covers the once-per-day rule.

usergames/telemetry.go:49-66: a failed tools/call (Go error or IsError result) writes an error record with e.Tool set, the account's player ID, and Message redacted (telemetry.Redact). usergames/telemetry.go:85-91 (BoardError) writes an error record with Action set (e.g. move) and the player ID; webui/actions.go:99-101 calls s.OnError on a failed action. Tests: usergames/telemetry_test.go:51-141 (failed import_log yields error with tool, message and player), cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_usage_test.go:165-184 (import_log error record and move error record each with player aID and a non-empty message), internal/webui/onerror_test.go:26-96.

No email ever reaches a record: telemetry/recorder.go:54 tags Email json:"-" and the line struct (recorder.go:64-75) has no email field; cut() (recorder.go:128-129, 168-189) removes the address from Message and Reason. Google tokens and display names are never passed to Record (hostauth/google.go:92-96, 230-231 pass only the account). Tool_call records have no Message field set. Error messages go through telemetry.Redact (redact.go:40-81) against the call's JSON arguments (SensitiveFromJSON, including battle-log lines and decklist card names, redact.go:196-233) and the caller's current game text (usergames/telemetry.go:97-146). cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_usage_test.go:186-228 checks the whole session's records and log for the email, display name, Google ID and access tokens, playmat tokens, cookie, each log line, and each deck card name, and internal/usergames/telemetry_test.go:143-168 checks redaction of game names. The redaction is heuristic, but the code and tests show the criterion holds for the scenarios covered.

cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go:134-138: a single AddReceivingMiddleware(a.MCPMiddleware(), reg.MCPMiddleware()) call, with a comment stating the ordering. In go-sdk v1.6.0 mcp/shared.go:88-92 addMiddleware iterates slices.Backward, so the first middleware is outermost. hostauth/limit.go:110-113 returns a tool error (IsError result, nil error) without calling next when over the limit, so the usergames tool-call middleware (usergames/telemetry.go:47-50) never runs for a refused call. The refusal is recorded as limited (hostauth/limit.go:85-87, reason rate). cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_usage_test.go:271-289 (TestHostedRateLimitRecordedOnce) asserts one limited record and no tool_call or error record for the refused call.

items.title: Let admins look up a player's ID

goal.title: Let admins look up a player's ID
criteria: Signed in as an admin, entering a player's email shows the same player ID their records carry.
A signed-in non-admin is refused, and a signed-out caller is refused or sent to sign in, without seeing any ID.
A lookup posted from another site is refused.
The looked-up email address appears in no log line or record.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/cacheadmin/handler.go:58-64 trims the posted email and renders &Lookup{ID: s.PlayerID(player)}. cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go:161-166 sets svc.PlayerID = rec.ID, and internal/telemetry/recorder.go:124 writes the record's player field with the same r.ids.ID(e.Email) (ids.go:43-51 normalises case and whitespace identically). cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_admin_test.go:273-287 (TestHostedAdminPlayerLookup) posts ' Two@Example.com ' as an admin and asserts the page contains "+twoID+", where twoID is the constant in hosted_test.go:351-358 that the records are checked against.

cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go:220-222 mounts /admin and /admin/ only as a.RequireAdmin(admin.Handler()), so POST /admin/player is covered. internal/hostauth/admin.go:33-37 refuses a signed-out non-GET with 401 'sign in required' and redirects signed-out page loads to sign-in. admin.go:43-50 refuses a signed-in non-admin with 403 and a page with no ID. The test at hosted_admin_test.go:289-302 checks 'non-admin' gets 403 and 'signed out' gets 401, and that neither body contains twoID.

internal/hostauth/admin.go:52-57 refuses any non-GET/HEAD admin request that fails a.sameSite(r) with 403 'admin changes must come from the playmat', before next.ServeHTTP runs the lookup. The lookup is a POST, so it is covered. hosted_admin_test.go:296 sends the lookup with Origin https://evil.example and expects 403 with no ID in the body. I did not re-run the test.

The email arrives only in the POST form body (handler.go:58), never in a URL. servePlayer (handler.go:49-65) writes no log line. Its only record is Event{Name: AdminAction, Email: email(r), Action: "lookup"} (handler.go:63), which carries the admin's address, hashed to a player ID, not the looked-up one. The recorder never writes the Email field (recorder.go:54 json:"-", recorder.go:124 writes only the ID). The old hostauth/admin.go log lines that printed the admin email were replaced with records (admin.go:44, 53). hosted_admin_test.go:303-306 and cacheadmin/events_test.go:86-92 assert the looked-up address appears in neither the records nor the logs. The email is echoed in the HTML response (page.go:67), which is neither a log line nor a record.
